text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to examine the infant's abdomen for any visible peristaltic waves or distension, and I will also check for signs of dehydration. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops with no rectal gas strongly suggest Hirschsprung disease. I will perform a digital rectal exam to check for a tight anal sphincter and an empty rectum, followed by a suction rectal biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells. REQUEST TEST: Suction_Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.
